Elena — great questions. Per our call I've sketched three pragmatic allocation profiles and an activation cadence that balances cost and latency risk. Summary first, details below.

Quick summary (recommended path = Profile B):
- Profile A (Conservative / Pilot): 16 total GPUs (2 x 8-GPU nodes), min guaranteed = 8 GPUs, burst to 24 via pre-warmed standby; good for tight budget validation.
- Profile B (Recommended / Launch): 48 total GPUs (6 x 8-GPU nodes), min guaranteed = 24 GPUs, burst to 72 with warm standby and short-term on-demand; designed to handle 95th percentile bursts up to ~450 QPS with 95th latency <300ms.
- Profile C (Growth / SLA): 96+ GPUs (12 x 8-GPU nodes), min guaranteed = 48 GPUs, plus cross-region failover; for heavy production with SLA and sustained throughput.

Ramp & activation (example for Profile B):
1) Boot (week 0–2): Activate 24 GPUs (min guarantee) to validate inference patterns with a canary subset of traffic (10–20%).
2) Launch (week 3–8): Scale to 48 GPUs as pre-warmed capacity based on telemetry (token service QPS + model sequence distribution).
3) Stabilize (week 9–12): Observe load, keep 24–48 range via autoscaling thresholds, add surge runbooks for holiday spikes.

Warm standby & latency guardrails:
- Maintain 20–30% of total pool as pre-warmed KV-cache-bearing nodes to keep prefix latency low.
- Continuous batching tuned to 50–150ms batching window depending on duty cycle.

Fallback / overage behavior:
- If burst > provisioned: automatic fallback to a slightly lower-cost model variant (quantized) for non-critical routes; traffic-shedding policy for non-essential background calls.
- Emergency: cross-region overflow to our EU/secondary pool if US capacity saturated (requires mutual action on data residency).

Security/compliance notes: KMS integration is standard for Redwood Private. We will include key-rotation schedules and audit logs in the Private deployment sheet.

I've attached a short runbook and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) template. Vanessa — can you add pricing rows and a proposed minimum commitment cadence?

Best,
Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: PX-4827 — pricing scenarios & milestone MAP (draft)

Elena — looping in the pricing sheet and a more prescriptive MAP. Highlights: 
- Per-GPU economics (list price): $1,900 / GPU / month on Profile B baseline. Discount tiers applied at 48 and 96 GPU commitments.
- Min-guarantee delta: 24 -> 32 GPUs increases monthly run-rate by ~$15k (post-discount estimate). I'll attach the line-by-line workbook.
- Quality-safe fallback: quantized model variant (4-bit) typically reduces token throughput latency by ~10–20ms but can introduce subtle generation differences; for reranking we recommend keeping the full-precision model on the rerank tier and using quantized for non-ranking user prompts.
- KMS: we support cross-region key-wrapping; customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) available for Private.

Draft MAP milestones (calendar view):
- Week 0 (sign): Sign MAP + finalize SSO/KMS scope.
- Week 1–2 (pilot): Provision 24 GPUs, run smoke tests with canary traffic.
- Week 3–6 (scale): Move to 48 GPUs, integrate logging/trace hooks, enable cost telemetry.
- Week 7–8 (hardening): Performance tuning, runload up to 95th burst simulation.
- Week 9 (GA): Full production cutover.

Attachments: px4827-draft-map.xlsx (worksheets: pricing, milestones, runbook)
